text:
Mental health Recognized as Fundamental Human Right at Sharjah’s World Congress 2025
A global dialogue is reinforcing the critical understanding that mental health is not a privilege, but a fundamental human right, notably for individuals with disabilities. This consensus emerged during a session at the World Congress 2025 “We contain,” currently underway in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates, and continuing through September 17 at the Expo Center Sharjah.
Experts and specialists participating in the congress underscored that prioritizing mental well-being is essential for ensuring quality education, healthcare, and social inclusion. The session, titled “Mental Health is a right not to choose,” brought together leading psychologists and behavioral experts to address the challenges and opportunities in safeguarding psychological safety.
Addressing Psychological Challenges in education
Psychological safety is paramount, particularly for students navigating mental disabilities. According to one speaker, students with mental disabilities often experience anxiety, depression, and diminished self-confidence, all of which can significantly impede academic performance and social development. Compounding these challenges, studies indicate a high co-occurrence of psychological disorders within this population: approximately 70% of individuals with autism spectrum disorder experience at least one concurrent psychological condition, with 40% facing multiple disorders.
This data highlights the urgent need for targeted treatment and behavioral interventions. Experts emphasized the effectiveness of behavioral cognitive therapy and strategies focused on supporting positive behavior as pivotal tools for fostering emotional resilience and developing well-rounded personalities capable of overcoming obstacles.
The Crucial Role of Family and Community Support
Beyond clinical interventions, a supportive ecosystem is vital. A senior official stressed that psychological safety is “not a luxury, but a necessity” for upholding the dignity and rights of persons with disabilities in all aspects of life – education, healthcare, and leisure. Family and community networks play a critical role in promoting mental health through environments built on respect, support, and awareness.
The Sharjah Human Services City was highlighted as a model for innovative support, including the provision of adapted sports equipment. This initiative aims to empower students to excel in activities they enjoy, reducing aggressive behaviors and fostering positive social interactions.
Empowering Through Positive Culture and Self-Reliance
Building a positive societal culture rooted in strong relationships and mutual trust is also essential. One expert cautioned against overprotection, arguing that excessive attention can inadvertently limit opportunities for learning and self-reliance. True empowerment, they asserted, requires an educational environment characterized by care, respect, and choice – one that cultivates independence and ensures active participation in society.
The session also featured motivational initiatives, such as “I am the hero of my story,” which utilizes storytelling to build values, develop personality, and enhance dialogue skills. The inclusion of parents sharing their personal experiences with their children added a powerful and relatable dimension to the discussion.
